purpose: Bounded Fair Work Commission case summary preserving a same-episode employment loss, alternative job, lower remuneration and travel burden, and ordered compensation without treating the order as payment receipt.

events.geography: Australia; public Fair Work Commission Bulletin Volume 4/25, item 3; drive-in/drive-out mining employment case
events.date_precision: bulletin publication date; underlying site-access revocation and termination occurred in September 2024, and alternative employment began three weeks after dismissal
events.denominator: One publicly summarized adjudicated case; no population denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the official Fair Work Commission bulletin summary of the merits and compensation decision
events.missingness: Applicant identity, exact dismissal date, alternative-employment employer, wage comparison, compensation payment receipt, household outcome, trust, collective action, recurrence, and exit are not reported
events.exposure: A mining contractor's client revoked the worker's site clearance after attendance and performance concerns; the contractor terminated the worker after finding no suitable nearby redeployment
events.alternatives_before_action: The worker obtained new employment three weeks after dismissal; the new job paid less and required significant personal travel costs, while the public record does not report other offers or a non-use option
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The worker experienced loss of the original site-based job, lower remuneration in the replacement job, and significant personal travel costs; the Commission assessed compensation at $18,192 plus superannuation
events.choice_or_response: The worker responded to the show-cause process, pursued an unfair-dismissal application, declined or did not seek reinstatement, and mitigated loss through lower-paid alternative employment
events.person_or_actor_with_control: The client controlled site clearance, the employer controlled termination and redeployment efforts, and the Commission controlled the adjudicated remedy
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The Commission found the dismissal harsh and unreasonable and ordered $18,192 plus superannuation compensation; the employer's attempted redeployment and the client's clearance decision remained separate control points
events.immediate_outcome: Alternative employment and a compensation order are reported in the same case, but compensation receipt and restoration of the original job are not observed
events.protected_outcome: The alternative job provided continued employment after dismissal, while the remedy order recognized a remaining income loss
events.sacrificed_outcome: The worker sacrificed remuneration and incurred travel costs relative to the original job; the public summary does not quantify the full household or time burden
events.cost_risk_transfer: The worker initially carried lower pay and travel costs; the compensation order shifted a bounded portion of assessed loss toward the employer, subject to payment execution
events.later_outcome: Alternative employment is observed, but its duration, later earnings, compensation receipt, household recovery, recurrence, trust, action, switching, and exit are unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: The decision attributes control across client clearance, employer termination, and Commission remedy, but contains no worker-reported trust, dignity, identity, or political-action endpoint
events.public_or_collective_response: An individual unfair-dismissal application and adjudicated compensation order are observed; no later collective or political response is reported
events.counterexample: A worker can obtain alternative employment and still experience lower pay and travel burdens; a compensation order does not prove payment or erase the original opportunity loss
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official Fair Work Commission Bulletin Volume 4/25, published April 3, 2025, item 3, https://www.fwc.gov.au/documents/bulletin/bulletin-ending-2025-03-31.htm; bulletin summary is public and bounded, with no underlying claimant file or payment receipt

arrows.evidence: The official bulletin reports termination after site-clearance revocation and new employment three weeks later at lower remuneration
arrows.counterexample: Obtaining a replacement job does not show that it was equivalent, freely chosen among viable options, or sufficient to restore income
arrows.remaining_gap: Alternative offers, search effort, timing, wage comparison, non-use option, and household constraints

arrows.evidence: The bulletin reports lower salary and significant personal travel costs in the new employment
arrows.counterexample: The public summary does not quantify net income, hours, expenses, or whether the alternative remained available
arrows.remaining_gap: Comparable wage, net costs, hours/control, duration, and household/time incidence

arrows.evidence: The Commission found the dismissal harsh and unreasonable and ordered $18,192 plus superannuation
arrows.counterexample: An ordered amount is not payment receipt, net recovery, or restoration of the original job
arrows.remaining_gap: Payment date/channel, receipt, taxation, residual loss, and implementation

arrows.to: household recovery, trust, action, recurrence, or exit
arrows.evidence: The public bulletin ends at the alternative-employment and compensation stages and reports no later household, trust, recurrence, action, or exit endpoint
arrows.counterexample: Replacement employment and an ordered remedy can coexist with persistent income, travel, or institutional-trust loss
arrows.remaining_gap: Receipt, duration, household recovery, later meaning/trust, recurrence, collective action, switching, and exit

boundary: This ledger adds one public case with an observed alternative-employment outcome and material trade-off in the same episode as an adjudicated compensation remedy. It does not establish payment receipt, full recovery, prevalence, trust, action, recurrence, or exit.
storage_boundary: No claimant file, direct identifier, bulk archive, or payment instrument is retained; only the bounded official bulletin summary, dates, reported employment transition, remedy amount, uncertainty, and open downstream arrow are represented.
